item.abstract: 豆姐威武！豆包工作上新21個專業工作臺，AI直接替你上班 聽雨 2026-11-23 10:29:24 來源： 量子位 豆包工作是目前位元組優先順序最高的產品 聽雨 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號QbitAI 去不了位元組打工，現在可以讓位元組的AI給你打工了。 豆包工作把這套能力開放了出來，最近上線的新功能 「工作臺」 ，一口氣鋪開21個專業場景。 從金融投研、創意設計，到醫療、教育，各有各的工作空間，預先配置了相應的技能和工具。 相當於你要找個幫手，豆包工作先替你把崗位分好、工具備齊，再由你來派活。 豆包工作上線三個月，DAU突破800萬，企業客戶ARR突破20億元。有業內人士告訴量子位，豆包工作目前是位元組優先順序最高的產品。 那麼，它剛上的新功能「工作臺」，到底能幹到哪一步？ 我們挑了 金融投研、創意設計、醫生和教師 四個工作臺進行實測，挨個交真實任務，自己看結果。 先說結論：按這次實測的表現，我們願意給80分。豆包工作已經能交出有用的工作底稿，值得專業人士繼續往下做。 比如，設計工作臺能連續完成電商主圖、海報和局部修改；教師工作臺寫教案時，還會提前列出學生容易犯的錯，配上老師可以追問的問題。 當然，素材裡的事實需要稽核，專業判斷以及成品能否交付，都需要人來拍板。 那麼，這80分是怎麼打出來的？我們實測走起～ 實測豆包工作的「工作臺」：四個職業測下來，它是幫手，不是替身 開啟豆包工作，左側選擇「外掛·技能·工作臺」，即可進入工作臺頁面。 裡面覆蓋了不同職業和任務的工作臺，包括金融投研、營銷、創意設計、教師、寫作、醫生等等。 點選「使用」即可將主頁面切換到工作臺頁面，左側也會把相應工作臺置頂。 金融投研工作臺：財報裡有的數字抄得準，沒有的它也不瞎編 進入金融投研工作臺，首頁就是個股分析、公告解讀、行業分析、市場簡報、公司研究這些入口。 需要資料時，在聯結器裡授權萬得、同花順、國泰海通等資料來源，就能直接呼叫。 具體怎麼用？玩法可簡可繁，技能和資料來源可以搭配使用。 比如我選擇「同花順iFinD金融分析」技能，再連線「同花順iFinD」資料來源，讓它做個股研究。 我們拿 輝達最新財報 試試。 這份財報11月18日凌晨剛剛釋出，營收1158億美元、同比翻倍，還是黃仁勳辭任後的首份財報。 把公告原文貼進去，問四個問題： 這財報說了啥？好訊息還是壞訊息？對股價可能有啥影響？還有啥沒搞明白的？ 用時11分半，好傢伙，豆包工作直接交出了一份財報解讀的html檔案。 報告開頭就給出判斷： 好訊息在收入，壞訊息在利潤率與現金流向。 有哪些依據？我們挑三處來看。 第一，豆包工作留意到，輝達這個財季多了一週。 它在報告裡列了四項資料：輝達營收1158億美元、淨利潤約653億美元、資料中心收入1076億美元、非GAAP毛利率74.9%。 我們對照財報逐項核了一遍，四個數字都對得上。 它還注意到，Q4營收指引包含額外一週。表面看環比增長12.2%，按兩個季度分別14周、13周折算，周均營收增幅約4.2%。這一步提醒了讀者：前後兩個數，不能直接比。 第二，補了來源，卻沒完全按要求來。 我們要求「沒寫就寫未披露」，它還是補進了1093.3億美元的營收預期、2.47美元的每股收益預期。 這些數字標了媒體轉引等出處，也提醒了不同來源的口徑差異。採購承諾的幾個數字口徑不一，它也沒有直接加總。 資訊有參考價值，但沒有遵守提示詞，這點得扣分。 第三，答不了的問題，單獨列了出來。 「2.5萬億美元積壓訂單」標了管理層口徑，業務拆分註明來自電話會。報告還列出七個未回答的問題，包括毛利率下滑的原因拆分、應收賬款賬齡等，末尾明確不輸出評級和目標價。 整體看，核過的幾項數字和計算能對上，來源也做了區分。 不過，轉引連結還沒逐條核實。這份報告可以拿來打底，補進來的資訊仍要查過再用。 最後一個小提醒： 用金融投研工作臺，提問時技能可以掛多個，資料來源也能掛多個。 如果光掛技能不掛資料來源，它就只能靠通用知識，調用不了真實資料。 創意設計工作臺：4張圖出一整套海報，改完還替你多看一眼 金融看完，我們再換個畫風完全不同的—— 創意設計工作臺 。 這個工作臺把電商產品圖、海報設計、社媒配圖、品牌設計、創意影片都放在一起。 任務一開，右邊自動建一塊畫布，生成的東西全落在上面，接著做下一個也不用重新上傳素材。 我們先試試讓它做 電商主圖 。 我上傳了3張咖啡素材：一把豆子的特寫、一個手衝場景、一個禮盒。 先讓它出5張1：1電商主圖，要求5張方向明顯不同、不能只是換背景： 請結合這3張參考圖，為一款精品咖啡豆生成5張1：1電商主圖，每張帶中文營銷文案。 要求：5張創意方向明顯不同 （視角、構圖、場景、排版、視覺重點都要變） ，不能只是同一張圖換背景；整體保持統一品牌調性；產品真實自然，不要塑膠感。 結果出來了，耗時4分01秒。 5張圖一次出齊。做電商AI圖一個常見的翻車點在於，同一張商品圖反覆換背景，5張看著很熱鬧，其實是同一張圖。 而 它真沒換背景偷懶， 五張硬是分成了五個方向： 豆堆首圖認貨、豆粒微距見品質、手衝場景賣氛圍、禮盒陳列講送禮、成品飲品給最終畫面。 齊活了，從原料一路喝進嘴裡。 再逐字核對文案：沒有錯字。「粒粒油亮」「精緻禮盒裝」這類文案全對，也沒混進價格、極限詞這類電商合規雷區。 不過現在的AI生圖，四到六個字的中文短句也基本不會出錯。如果字數一多、數字混排、密集小字就容易翻車。 但解決方法也很簡單，你可以直接點選海報，在右側手動修改。 回到這套交付結果，我覺得它真正的缺點在於：短句能一次出對，並不等於整張海報能直接用。 AI生成的文案全是「深烘醇厚」「餘韻悠長」這類通用賣點，真要上架，產地、烘焙度、規格還是得自己補。 接下來繼續讓它 用主圖出海報 。不新開任務，我們又補充了一句： 用剛才的素材，再做3張3：4豎版海報，分別突出「新豆上市」「產地/風味」「節日禮贈」。 3張一次出齊，風格跟主圖相匹配，一眼能看出是同一款產品。 更值得注意的是，產地那張沒寫國家、莊園、海拔。素材裡沒依據，它寧可留白也不虛標，相當於幫你繞開了虛標的合規風險。 海報確實做得還可以，但我們還得再測測 改圖 。繼續輸入提示詞： 把「新豆上市」那張頂部的標題換成「深烘醇厚 新豆上市」，其他一個字、一個元素都別動。 41秒改完，只花掉賬號額度的0.31% （這是佔總額度的比例，隨套餐額度池大小而變） 。 結果比我們預期的要好。標題按要求修改了，其餘豆堆、杯子、副標題、標籤、光影、背景，也全部保持原樣。 而且它不只改對了，還自己挑出了一個我們沒注意的問題： 右下角標籤仍寫著深烘醇厚，與主標題首行重複。 感覺就像是有個設計助理替你多看了一眼，做電商的都懂，海報上一個詞重複兩遍有多掉價…… 值得注意的是， Seedream 5.5 於11月9日釋出，官方明確說同步上線豆包、豆包工作、即夢。 在豆包工作裡通過「技能」入口呼叫，豆包工作中的社媒配圖、風格海報這類內建技能會直接呼叫它。 所以以上生成的海報，大機率就走這個模型。 醫生工作臺：不替醫生拍板，也不把患者嚇回去 醫生工作臺首頁有六個入口： 臨床診療與循證、醫學文獻檢索、醫學教學與彙報總結、用藥查詢與處方稽核、醫學科普與患者溝通、醫學科研與論文。 頁面明確標註： 僅供科研輔助，不替代執業醫師臨床判斷 。 所以這輪測試，我們主要讓它查藥物相互作用和診療依據。 同時看看：資訊不全時，它會怎樣回答；面對不同的提問方式，又會怎樣提示使用邊界。 Case 1：查藥物相互作用 （測準不準+會不會編） 我們先問了一個用藥問題： 長期吃甲氨蝶呤的類風溼患者，尿路感染能不能用複方磺胺甲噁唑？ 這個問題涉及兩種藥物合用的嚴重風險。我們想看它能否解釋相互作用機制，提供文獻依據，以及會不會直接替醫生定方案。 2分43秒後，報告出來了。 它從腎小管排洩競爭、葉酸通路雙重阻斷等機制講起，引用了FDA標籤、藥品說明書、指南和病例報告，還標出了Grade C/Level 4等證據等級。 報告給出的方向是「避免合用」，並列出了它引用的藥品說明書依據。 不過，讓我們意外的有兩點： 一是它戳破了一個想當然。 很多人以為，把兩種藥錯開幾小時吃就安全了。 它直接否掉：錯開吃藥時間沒用，因為問題出在清除率下降和抗葉酸效應疊加，不是吸收環節的螯合。 二是它主動交底。 這個病人沒給劑量、腎功能、合併用藥，結論只能到「避免合用」；補上這些資訊，可能就變成「明確禁忌」。它把「我不知道」明明白白寫出來，還告訴你缺的資訊會怎麼改變答案。 從始至終，它沒下一句醫囑。給的全是「循證處置方向」，反覆標註「僅供處方醫師參考，不構成處方建議」。 還有一個小提醒：它引的那些指南和病例，格式、期刊、作者對得上，沒有編造跡象。 但報告裡的連結我們沒有逐條開啟核實。它自己也在末尾附了來源清單，大家可以自己去查。 Case 2：同一個問題，兩種問法 （測是否「看人下菜碟」） 我們用醫生和患者兩種不同角度來問豆包工作，看它會不會看人下菜碟。 先用一個普通患者的口吻問： 體檢發現右肺6mm純磨玻璃結節，邊界清楚。網上說可能是早期肺癌，我是不是該儘快手術切掉？ 它開口先糾偏：6mm不屬於「該儘快切掉」，網上「磨玻璃＝早期肺癌」的說法省略了後半句——這類結節長得慢，觀察幾年再決定並不吃虧。 然後給的東西相當專業：三份指南對照表 （Fleischner 2017、中國專家共識2024、胸外科共識2024） ，6mm落在「隨訪觀察」區間，離手術門檻 （>10mm） 還差著。 還講了倍增時間、5年增大比例、哪幾種情況才需要升級處理。 item.title: How to Use AI Tools to Learn Data Science Faster in 2026
item.abstract: How to Use AI Tools to Learn Data Science Faster in 2026 Discover how to combine AI assistants, coding tools, and adaptive platforms to cut your learning curve and build practical skills more efficiently. By Vinod Chugani on November 23, 2026 in Data Science Learning data science is more accessible now than it's ever been, and AI tools are a big reason why. Where students once spent days debugging a single script or searching through documentation, they can now get instant, context-aware explanations and code suggestions in seconds. But that accessibility comes with a catch. he best AI tools in 2026 reduce friction across the whole learning process. The best ones reduce friction across the entire learning process. The real question is which ones to use, and how to use them without letting them do all the thinking for you. The real question is which ones to use, and how to use them without letting them do all the thinking for you. This guide walks through practical strategies for using AI tools at every stage of data science learning, from building Python foundations to preparing for your first data science role. Getting the Foundation Right First Before reaching for any AI tool, there's one principle worth establishing: don't learn AI before you learn analytics fundamentals. This matters because AI assistants are most useful when you already have enough context to evaluate what they're telling you. If you ask an AI to explain a confusion matrix and you've never studied classification, the explanation will be surface-level at best and misleading at worst. Start by building a working knowledge of Python, basic statistics, and data manipulation with libraries like pandas and NumPy . Once you have that grounding, AI tools become multipliers rather than crutches. Use them to go deeper, not to skip steps. A solid starting point for structured learning is DataCamp , which offers an AI-native format with adaptive tutoring that adjusts to your skill level, pace, and context in real time. That kind of responsive feedback is especially useful early on, when misconceptions tend to compound if left uncorrected. Using AI Assistants as On-Demand Tutors With a foundation in place, conversational AI assistants become some of the most useful learning tools you have. Tools like ChatGPT and Copilot can answer coding questions, break down complex concepts, and generate code snippets on demand. No office hours, no waiting. The key is treating them as a thinking partner rather than a search engine. Instead of pasting an error and asking for a fix, describe what you were trying to accomplish, explain what you tried, and ask the assistant to walk you through what went wrong. That keeps you in the driver's seat while still getting the help you need. Three concrete techniques worth trying during self-study: Concept deep-dives. Ask the assistant to explain a concept multiple ways, then follow up until it clicks. If you're struggling with gradient descent, ask for a visual analogy, then ask how the learning rate affects convergence, then ask for a minimal Python implementation. Code review. Paste your own code and ask for feedback. Not just "is this correct?" but "what would an experienced data scientist change about this, and why?" Study planning. Share your current skill level and your learning goal (say, preparing for a machine learning role at a mid-size company) and ask the assistant to build a weekly study plan with specific resources and milestones. Accelerating Coding with AI Coding Assistants One of the biggest time sinks in learning data science is the gap between understanding a concept and being able to implement it cleanly in code. AI coding assistants close that gap. For learners specifically, the benefit isn't just speed. It's the ability to see idiomatic, well-structured code alongside your own attempts, which trains your eye for quality over time. GitHub Copilot is the most widely recommended option for data science contexts. Development teams using it report around 40% productivity gains on average, and for learners building portfolio projects, that speed translates directly into more finished work. That matters a lot for job seekers. Cursor is another tool gaining traction, particularly for developers who want tighter control over how AI suggestions are integrated into their workflow. When using a coding assistant for learning, don't accept every suggestion automatically. Treat each one as a prompt: do I understand why this code works? If not, ask the assistant to explain it line by line. That turns passive code generation into active learning. Here's a simple workflow for working through a new concept: # Step 1: Write your own attempt first import pandas as pd df = pd.read_csv('sales_data.csv') monthly = df.groupby('month')['revenue'].sum() print(monthly) This calculates monthly revenue totals from a sales dataset. # Step 2: Ask the assistant to suggest improvements # Copilot or ChatGPT might suggest: monthly = ( df.groupby('month')['revenue'] .sum() .reset_index() .rename(columns={'revenue': 'total_revenue'}) ) Comparing both versions and asking why the second approach is preferred builds intuition faster than tutorials alone. Building Projects with AI Guidance Portfolio projects are still the most effective way to demonstrate data science skills to employers. AI tools have made it easier to scope and execute them well. Most learners struggle more with direction than motivation. What dataset? What question? What level of complexity? AI assistants can help you answer all three, then serve as a sounding board as you build. A practical approach: describe your current skill level and target role to an AI assistant and ask it to suggest three portfolio project ideas that demonstrate relevant competencies. Once you pick one, ask it to help outline the project structure, including what exploratory data analysis to run, what models to try, and how to frame your findings. From there, use the assistant as you go. When you get stuck on a visualization, describe what you're trying to show and ask for suggestions. When model performance is lower than expected, ask for a systematic list of things to investigate. Jupyter Notebook remains the standard environment for this kind of exploratory work. Many AI assistants integrate directly with Jupyter through extensions, so you can get help without leaving your workflow. Using AI for Concept Reinforcement and Self-Testing One often-overlooked use of AI tools is active recall, one of the most well-supported learning techniques around. Instead of re-reading notes, ask an AI assistant to quiz you. A prompt like "Quiz me on the difference between bagging and boosting. Ask me five questions, one at a time, and tell me if my answer is correct before moving on" turns a passive review session into active retrieval practice. You can extend this to code challenges. Ask the assistant for a machine learning problem with a dataset description and expected output, then try to write the solution before asking for hints. This mirrors the format of technical interviews and builds both skill and confidence. For learners using Dataquest or similar interactive platforms, the browser-based coding exercises already build in this active practice model. Pairing them with an AI assistant for the moments you're genuinely stuck, rather than at the first sign of difficulty, gives you the best of both. Staying Current with Emerging Tools and Research Data science moves fast, and AI tools help you keep up with less effort. In 2026, the role of the data scientist has shifted from "model builder" to "AI orchestrator." That means learners need to understand not just classical machine learning methods but also how to work with large language models, build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, and use frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex .

item.title: Amazon snaps up Decart’s AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips
item.abstract: Amazon has agreed to acquire a good chunk of Israeli startup Decart. The e-commerce and cloud giant is paying $7.5 billion for the startup, according to Bloomberg. Decart has made a name for itself building interactive real-time world models — most recently Oasis 3 — and AI video-generation tools. But under the hood, the company stands out for its Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), software that helps AI models run efficiently on Nvidia, Amazon, and Google’s hardware. As part of the deal, Amazon will acquire the technology behind DOS, as well as Decart’s founding team and team of AI researchers and engineers, Amazon said in a blog post . “Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip,” said Peter DeSantis, SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, quantum computing, at Amazon. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost.” Amazon, which has so far been using its Trainium chips at its own data centers, is preparing to start selling them to customers as a competitor to Nvidia. Decart’s technology could make it easier for customers to run their workloads on Amazon chips, rather than Nvidia’s, which has been the gold standard so far. Decart and Amazon did not immediately return requests for comment.

item.title: States sue SpaceX to stop Grok from generating child sex images, revenge porn
item.abstract: On Monday, Virginia and Oregon became the first states to sue SpaceX, alleging that Grok continues to sexualize, unchecked, real photos of mostly women and children. SpaceX acquired xAI in February and now must handle the ongoing reckoning over the controversial rollout of Grok’s “spicy mode”—a model feature Musk hyped but was soon found to generate a flood of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) and child sex abuse images (CSAM). Initial safeguards were so lax that Grok sometimes generated nude images without being asked . Although X Safety and xAI (now known as SpaceXSI) were silent at first , Musk’s companies eventually apologized and claimed that additional safeguards were implemented and policies redesigned to block harmful outputs. However, state attorneys general alleged that those statements were “misleading” and that SpaceXSI instead quietly “embraced” sexualized content to seize more AI market share, as Grok continues to generate NCII and CSAM today. Without intervention, kids in Virginia and Oregon risk a lifetime of distress, as Grok images will likely be impossible to remove online. “Once created and shared,” Grok-generated CSAM and NCII “can never be fully erased, and it becomes a permanent record of the child’s abuse that may resurface for the rest of the child’s life,” Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones’ complaint said. “Virginia has a profound interest in protecting its children from this harm.” Millions allegedly harmed Millions of residents were allegedly harmed, as the attorneys general seek to protect every Grok or X user in their state. Many Grok victims will likely suffer from chronic anxiety, depression, and PTSD, as well as reputational harm, as some viewers may not realize the images are AI-generated, the states alleged. Further—due to Grok’s integration with the social media platform X—users as young as 13 may have been exposed to the AI content and possibly re-traumatized if they, too, are victims of sexual abuse, the states alleged.
